Marius Petipa was a French-Russian choreographer who is the architect of classical ballet as we know it, having created the vocabulary, structure, and aesthetic that defined the nineteenth-century Russian Imperial Ballet. Born in eighteen eighteen in Marseille, he trained in Paris before immigrating to St. Petersburg in eighteen forty-seven to become the Imperial Ballet's principal choreographer. He held the position of Ballet Master of the Imperial Marinsky Theatre for over sixty years, creating nearly sixty ballets and becoming the de facto sovereign of Russian classical ballet. He collaborated with composer Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky on The Sleeping Beauty in eighteen ninety and The Nutcracker in eighteen ninety-two, creating the template for all full-length classical ballets. He choreographed the final act of Swan Lake and established the pas de deux as an architectural centerpiece of ballet, with its own prescribed structure: adagio, variations, coda. He perfected the classical ballet vocabulary we use today, codifying positions and the balletic use of the spine and turnout, and an aesthetic of verticality, extension, and aristocratic restraint. He also created a system of training adjacent to the Cecchetti method that standardized ballet instruction across Russia and later influenced the entire world. His ballets combine mathematical precision with profound musicality; his orchestration of ensemble work, like the Grand Pas de Quatre, remains unmatched.
